teachingQuestion: How do implementation attacks differ from a broken cryptographic primitive?
focalInsight: An attacker may learn or alter behavior through observable implementation signals; defense starts by identifying the signal, access, secret, and appropriate engineering or physical control.
title: Classify leakage and fault paths before choosing a defense
caption: The same sensitive operation can have remote error, timing, local runtime, and physical fault exposures.
altSummary: Implementation attacks require an observable signal or induced fault, attacker access, and a secret or state to infer or alter. Engineering and environmental controls reduce different parts of that path.
textFallback: Identify the observable timing, error, power, cache, electromagnetic, or other signal. Define whether an attacker is remote, local, co-resident, or physical. Identify the protected key, credential, or validation state. For faults, identify how input, memory, clock, voltage, or environmental disturbance could alter execution. Use vetted implementation, uniform errors, validation, protected hardware, controlled interfaces, update integrity, and monitoring as applicable.
